passages.title: Seeking without losing ourselves
passages.intro: What happens to our search when we turn away from our own nature? This short surviving phrase leaves the object of that search unnamed.
passages.boundaryStart: The excerpt begins within a damaged line; preceding writing is not reproduced here.
passages.boundaryEnd: The excerpt ends within line 6. The column continues; this is not the end of the argument.

english.text: We shall seek something, yet not obtain it,

modern.text: We can search for something and still fail to find it—

greek.text: ἐὰν τρόπον τινὰ ἑαυτῶν ἀπ̣οϲτῶ̣μεν καὶ τῆϲ φύϲεωϲ ἡμῶν,

english.text: if we somehow turn away from ourselves and our own nature.

modern.text: if we lose touch with ourselves and our own nature.

notes.title: Why leave “something” unspecified?
notes.text: The excerpt does not identify what is sought. We have not replaced it with happiness, truth or virtue.

notes.title: Why say “lose touch”?
notes.text: That is our interpretive wording for turning away from oneself, not an instruction to follow personal feelings.

notes.title: What do the tiny dots mean?
notes.text: A dot beneath a Greek letter marks an uncertain reading in the scholarly transcription. We retain those marks instead of silently making the text certain.
